hub.name: Fractions, one piece at a time

questions.prompt: Which is larger for the same whole?
questions.explanation: Both use sevenths; four such pieces exceed two.

questions.prompt: Which is larger: 1/2 or 1/4 of the same whole?
questions.explanation: Halves are larger pieces than quarters.
They are 8/12 and 9/12 respectively, so three quarters is larger.

title: Which fraction is bigger?
practice: Try a few problems at your own pace, then return to any explanation you want to revisit.

sections.html:
Take two identical chocolate bars. Split each bar into five equal pieces.

You get three pieces from one bar. A friend gets two pieces from the other. Your share is bigger because the pieces are the same size and you have one more.

We write those shares as 3/5 and 2/5. When the bottom numbers match and the wholes are the same size, compare the top numbers.
sections.title: Use the same starting size

sections.html:
Draw two strips of equal length. Divide one into two equal parts and the other into four. Shade one part of each strip. Which shaded piece is longer?

One half is larger even though two is smaller than four. With one selected part in each fraction, a larger denominator means the whole was split into more, smaller pieces. The bottom number is not a score where higher always wins.
sections.title: Try it yourself

sections.html:
Which is bigger: 2/3 or 3/4? The pieces are different sizes, so counting two pieces against three is not enough.

Draw two identical strips, each divided into twelve small equal pieces.

  1. On the first strip, one third covers four small pieces. Two thirds cover eight. Colour those eight pieces.
  2. On the second strip, one quarter covers three small pieces. Three quarters cover nine. Colour those nine pieces.
  3. Compare the coloured amounts. Nine small pieces cover more than eight.

So 3/4 is bigger than 2/3. We changed how we divided the strips, not the amounts we were comparing.
sections.title: Compare using matching pieces

sections.html:
Halfway is a useful place to start. Draw a strip with eight equal pieces. Four pieces cover half of it.

  • Three pieces do not reach halfway, so 3/8 is less than 1/2.
  • Five pieces go past halfway, so 5/8 is more than 1/2.

You do not need a new calculation each time. First ask where the coloured amount sits on the strip.
sections.title: Is it more or less than half?

description: Compare equal-size strips before relying on the written numbers, and learn two useful shortcuts.
